FS SKU #70361 - a sliding drawer with front access to patch cords and rear access to cable entry, holding up to four FHD fiber adapter panels or MTP/MPO cassettes for up to 144 fibers in 1U.","format":1,"gaps":[{"note":"the extraction handles and FS logo visible in the page-1 product photograph are real but undimensioned anywhere in the corpus - no page gives their position, and a perspective product shot is not a source panel_measure can rectify the way the FHD cassettes' face-on renders were. The front view here draws the four bays and the rack ears only. RE-READ when fs/fhd-splice-12-lc@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: that addition names a cassette that seats inside a bay, not the enclosure's own front panel, so it neither closes this gap nor opens a new one. RE-READ AGAIN when fs/fhd-2mtp12-lc-os2-a@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: same reasoning - a two-MTP cassette still seats inside a bay the same 108.97 x 35.05 way its one-MTP sibling does, so it neither closes this gap nor opens a new one either. RE-READ A THIRD TIME when fs/fhd-1mtp12-sc-os2-a@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: an SC cassette seats in the same 108.97 x 35.05 bay opening its LC and splice siblings do - its front connector family is different, its body is 7.62 mm deeper, but neither changes what the enclosure's own front panel around the bay looks like - so the gap stands unchanged a third time. RE-READ A FOURTH TIME when fs/fhd-1mtp24-lc-os2-a@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: an MTP-24 cassette seats in the same 108.97 x 35.05 bay opening its MTP-12 sibling does - its front is the identical twelve LC-duplex layout fs/fhd-2mtp12-lc-os2-a@1 already uses, and its rear carries a wider MPO ferrule the front panel never sees - so the gap stands unchanged a fourth time. RE-READ when every FHD LC and SC cassette's adapter row moved 1.4-1.8 mm right (fs/fhd-1mtp6lcd-os2-a@4 and its siblings), once `panel_measure` framed FS's renders on the plate's real edge rather than its rounded corner: the rows sit inside each cassette's own plate, not on the enclosure's front panel, so the gap stands unchanged. RE-READ when the LC and SC duplex adapters on the cassettes renamed their bores from tx and rx to fibre positions 1 and 2 and the cassettes composing them took a major: an addressing change inside the bay occupants, not on the front panel around them, so the gap stands unchanged. RE-READ when the fifteen FHD adapter panels joined every bay's `accepts`: a panel is a plate of adapters seated in the same 108.97 x 35.05 bay, so it changes what fills a bay, not the enclosure's own front around it - the gap stands.","reason":"needs-photo","scope":["front"],"wanted":"a square-on, face-on photograph of the closed FHD-1UFCE front, the same kind of image that let the cassettes' own faceplates be measured.","what":"front-panel-detail"},{"note":"these five faces carry the bare envelope box from the dimensioned `chassis` figures and nothing else - no slide rail, no cable-management arm, no screws, no rear opening for the cassettes' MTP trunks to pass through. Page 7 dimensions only the front and top outlines, and even the top view resolves no surface detail beyond its own outline. RE-READ when fs/fhd-splice-12-lc@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: a splice cassette's trunk fibres still leave through the same undimensioned rear opening this gap already names, so the gap stands unchanged rather than needing a second one for the new cassette. RE-READ AGAIN when fs/fhd-2mtp12-lc-os2-a@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: its two MTP trunks leave through the same undimensioned rear opening too - twice the trunks, not a different opening - so the gap stands unchanged a second time. RE-READ A THIRD TIME when fs/fhd-1mtp12-sc-os2-a@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: its single MTP trunk leaves through the same undimensioned rear opening its LC and splice siblings use - a deeper cassette body (117.86 mm against 110.24, as was then believed; every FHD cassette here is 117.86, the 110.24 having been a misreading corrected in fs/fhd-1mtp6lcd-os2-a@2), not a different rear opening - so the gap stands unchanged a third time. RE-READ A FOURTH TIME when fs/fhd-1mtp24-lc-os2-a@1 joined every bay's `accepts`: its single MTP-24 trunk leaves through the same undimensioned rear opening its MTP-12 siblings use - a wider ferrule on one trunk instead of two narrower ones, not a different opening, and the same 117.86 mm body depth fs/fhd-2mtp12-lc-os2-a@1 already carries - so the gap stands unchanged a fourth time. NARROWED, NOT CLOSED, when the rear gained its opening: the owner of the model reports the back is open behind the slots, so the rear now draws one hole per bay and the cassettes' backs through it (see `provenance.rear-opening`). What the report cannot give is the opening's real outline - four holes or one, the bay's size or not - and nothing held shows the rear, so the photograph is still wanted. RE-READ when the Type AF and universal cassettes (57037, 68540, 68549, 182641, 182643) joined every bay's `accepts`: they are their Type A twins' bodies with different internal wiring and rear labels, so their trunks leave through the same undimensioned opening - the gap stands. RE-READ when the OM3, OM4, OM5 and OM4 universal cassettes (57017, 57342, 57024, 174246, 174248, 174250, 182642, 182644, 382889, 382897) joined every bay's `accepts`: they are their OS2 twins' bodies in another fibre with other-coloured adapters, and their rear renders - 57017.E, 57342.E, 57024.E and the g4 views of the other seven - print the same port-range legends and Type A labels on the same MTP bulkheads (the lid-edge seal sticker reads differently on the 2025-26 renders and is not drawn), so their trunks leave through the same undimensioned opening - the gap stands. RE-READ when the 36-fibre cassettes (105333, 105335) joined every bay's `accepts`: three MTP trunks instead of one or two, leaving through the same undimensioned rear opening from the same 99 x 31 body - the gap stands. RE-READ when every FHD LC and SC cassette's adapter row moved 1.4-1.8 mm right on its faceplate: a front-plate change, which none of these five faces shows - the gap stands. RE-READ when each rear MPO adapter gained its fibre elements, 1 to 12 or 1 to 24: they sit on the cassette rear, and the rear opening the trunks leave through is as undimensioned as it was - the gap stands. RE-READ when the bays stopped saying where a back lands (`rear.at`) and each back began landing where its own module's body stands, mirrored in the hole: the holes and the opening are unchanged, and nothing held shows them any better - the gap stands. RE-READ when the fifteen FHD adapter panels joined every bay's `accepts`: a panel's rear is its adapters' far ends, 16 to 32 deep instead of a 117.86 cassette body, and the cords reach them through the same undimensioned opening - the gap stands.","reason":"needs-photo","scope":["rear","top","bottom","left","right"],"wanted":"a rear photograph (the cassettes seat from the front but the trunk cables leave from the back of the drawer) and a lid/side photograph, the same kind of source dcp-2's own equivalent gap asks for.","what":"envelope-face-detail"}],"groups":{"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"slots":{"description":"four slots, each taking one FHD module - a fiber adapter panel or an MTP/MPO cassette. The datasheet's capacity row for #70361 reads \"4 ports\"; the features list adds \"holds up to 4x FAPs or MTP\u00ae Cassettes\".","index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"Slot"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"FS.com","maturity":"modelled","model":"FHD-1UFCE","name":"fhd-1ufce","profile":"optical","provenance":{"bays":{"note":"FOUR IS COUNTED, NOT MEASURED. The capacity table's \"4 ports\" and the features list's \"holds up to 4x FAPs or MTP\u00ae Cassettes\" agree on the number; no page in this datasheet dimensions an empty bay opening. Each bay is sized at 108.97 x 35.05 - the FHD module envelope, a FAMILY CONSTANT common to every cassette this format admits, not a figure this device measures itself or that belongs to any one cassette. It was first measured off FS's own render for fs/fhd-1mtp6lcd-os2-a@4 (SKU 57016), and `panel_measure` refuses to scale ANY FHD face-on render at all unless that scale reproduces the same 35.05mm height - which is what makes this a constant worth carrying rather than a per-cassette reading. THE RULE, NOT A COUNT: every FHD cassette this library models seats in every bay's `accepts`, because the FHD format defines one shared envelope for the slot rather than a per-cassette one - see each bay's own `accepts` list below for which cassettes that is today. The bay geometry does not depend on which of them seats in it, because every FHD module this plan might still add shares this one envelope by definition of the format (the format's own name for it). The four bays sit contiguous across the panel: (448.0 - 4 x 108.97) / 2 = 6.06mm margin each side, centred top-to-bottom in the 44.0mm face: (44.0 - 35.05) / 2 = 4.475mm. THE ADAPTER PANELS JOINED IN 5.1.0: fifteen FHD panels (LC 24F in OS2 UPC and APC, OM4 and OM5; LC 36F in OS2 and OM4; SC in OS2 UPC and APC and OM4; three MTP and one MTP-16; the multimedia modular panel and the blank) are in every bay's `accepts`. They are class adapter-panel, not cassette, so the cassette-envelope rule does not reach them; FS states the compatibility itself - every FHD enclosure datasheet (1UFMT-N, 1UFMT-S, 1UME, the slide-out family) says it takes all FHD cassettes and panels, and each prints the same loading list with the panels on it."},"chassis":{"note":"page 7, front view: 448.0mm (17.64in) body width, dimensioned on its own line below the 482.6mm (19in) rack-width line - two separate dimensions, not one measured against the other. 44.0mm (1.73in) height, the only figure on that view's right edge. Page 7, top view: 432.8mm (17.04in) depth. All three also appear in the spec table on the same page - \"Dimensions (HxWxD): 1.73\"x19\"x17.04\" (44x482.6x432.8mm)\" - which is what corroborates the drawing rather than the other way round. `ru: 1` from that same table's \"No. of Rack Spaces: 1U\"."},"ears":{"note":"482.6mm (19in) on the same front-view dimension line as the 448.0mm body - the standard EIA-310 rack width. Drawn as common/rack-ear@1 outside the body under the optional tag `ears`, the same generic ear every other 19in device in this library uses; its own 14.0mm width is that component's convention, not a second measurement of this drawing."},"envelope-faces":{"note":"rear, top, bottom, left and right carry the ENVELOPE ONLY, the same treatment dcp-2 gives the four sides no photograph resolved. Top and bottom are 448.0 x 432.8 and left/right are 432.8 x 44.0 - both pairs built from the same `chassis` figures already sourced above, not a second measurement. No surface detail (screws, the slide rail, the cable-management arm the 467.2mm overall depth implies) is drawn on any of the five; see `gaps` below. THE REAR IS NOW THE EXCEPTION: it carries the open back behind each slot - see `rear-opening`."},"front-panel-detail":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"ESTIMATED BY OMISSION. Page 1's product photograph shows two extraction handles near the panel ends and an FS logo left of centre, but page 7's dimensioned drawing - the only source this device transcribes figures from - locates none of them, and a three-quarter photograph is not a source panel_measure can rectify. None of that detail is drawn; see `gaps` below."},"method":{"note":"FIGURES FIRST, FROM THE VENDOR'S OWN DIMENSIONED DRAWING. Every number in `chassis` below is read directly off page 7 of working/intake/fs/fhd/datasheets/fhd-1ufce-fiber-enclosure-datasheet.pdf, which carries a dimensioned front view and a dimensioned top view of this exact part - the only page in the corpus that dimensions anything. Nothing else about this device is measured; what is not on that page is estimated and said so below, or left undrawn."},"model":{"note":"the datasheet's own \"Fiber Enclosure Capacity\" table names #70361 as the ordering ID for \"FHD 1U slide-out rack mount enclosure\", model FHD-1UFCE, \"4 ports\", \"144F\". The features list on page 1 adds \"Mounts to standard EIA 19\" rack rails, holds up to 4x FAPs or MTP\u00ae Cassettes.\""},"overall-depth":{"note":"the top view carries a second, larger depth line outside the 432.8mm body - 467.2mm (18.39in). That is the envelope INCLUDING whatever projects from the rear (the drawer's cable-management arm, most likely), not the body depth, and the spec table's own HxWxD row confirms 432.8 as the figure it means by \"depth\". Recorded here because the drawing shows it; not used as `chassis.depth`, which the two agreeing sources both give as 432.8."},"rear-opening":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"REPORTED, NOT PHOTOGRAPHED. The owner of this model reports that the drawer's back is open behind the slots, a hole roughly the size of a cassette faceplate through which the cassettes' backs and MTP trunks are seen and reached - which is what the trunk cables leaving from the back of the drawer need. No image held shows the rear; every FS photograph of 70361 is of the front, the door or the pulled-out drawer. So the four holes are each the front bay's own 108.97 x 35.05 at the bay's own height, mirrored left to right because the back is seen from behind; their real outline, and whether it is one hole or four, is still open (the `envelope-face-detail` gap). Each runs 431.8 in - the 432.8 drawer less a 1.0 front plate, which is ESTIMATED - so the slot is a passage the cassette's own 117.86 mm body stands in, open front to back when it is out. WHERE IN THE HOLE a back is drawn is the seated module's: its `body.footprint`, mirrored across the bay - a cassette's 99 x 31 body and an adapter panel's 88 x 34.8 one both centre in the hole, from two different offsets - so no bay states
